objects.description: Enumeration of common AOM codec control identifiers used with encoder/decoder control interfaces. Values 230–255 are reserved for common controls; AOM_DECODER_CTRL_ID_START marks the start of decoder-only IDs. Used to select specific control operations such as getting/setting AV1 reference frames and accessing the new frame image.

AV1-specific reference frame data structure used to pass reference frame information to/from codec controls. Fields: idx selects the reference frame index; use_external_ref indicates decoder should directly use an external reference buffer; img is an aom_image_t populated when getting/copying reference frames. Note: aom_image_t is defined in aom/aom_image.h and is not defined here.

functions.name: aom_uleb_size_in_bytes
functions.description: Computes the number of bytes required to encode an unsigned 64-bit integer using the LEB128 (unsigned) variable-length format. Useful for sizing buffers prior to encoding.
requirements: Argument value may be any uint64_t; there are no documented restrictions.
Caller should use the returned size to provision sufficient space if subsequently encoding the same value.

functions.name: aom_uleb_decode
functions.signature: int aom_uleb_decode(const uint8_t *buffer, size_t available, uint64_t *value, size_t *length);
functions.description: Decodes an unsigned LEB128 value from a byte buffer. On success, writes the decoded value to value and the number of bytes consumed to length. Returns 0 on success, -1 on decode failure (e.g., malformed or incomplete LEB128 within the provided byte count). Intended for length-bounded parsing of ULEB128 streams.
requirements: buffer must point to a memory region containing at least available bytes accessible for reading.
available specifies the maximum number of bytes the function may read; it may be 0 (in which case decoding will fail).
value must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the decoded integer on success.
length must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes consumed on success.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates decode failure and value/length are not guaranteed to be meaningful.
On success, *length will be the exact number of bytes consumed and will be <= available.

functions.name: aom_uleb_encode
functions.signature: int aom_uleb_encode(uint64_t value, size_t available, uint8_t *coded_value, size_t *coded_size);
functions.description: Encodes an unsigned 64-bit integer into LEB128 format. Writes the encoded bytes into coded_value up to the provided capacity and returns the number of bytes written via coded_size. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure (e.g., insufficient space).
requirements: coded_value must point to a writable buffer with at least available bytes of capacity.
available specifies the maximum number of bytes that may be written; must be sufficient for the LEB128 encoding of value.
coded_size must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of bytes written on success.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure and coded_size/coded_value contents are not guaranteed to be meaningful.
On success, *coded_size will be the exact number of bytes written and will be <= available.

functions.name: aom_uleb_encode_fixed_size
functions.signature: int aom_uleb_encode_fixed_size(uint64_t value, size_t available, size_t pad_to_size, uint8_t *coded_value, size_t *coded_size);
functions.description: Encodes an unsigned 64-bit integer into LEB128 using exactly pad_to_size bytes. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure (e.g., the value cannot be represented in the requested fixed size or capacity is insufficient). On success, writes exactly pad_to_size bytes to coded_value and sets coded_size accordingly.
requirements: coded_value must point to a writable buffer with at least available bytes accessible; to succeed, it must have at least pad_to_size bytes of capacity.
available specifies the maximum number of bytes that may be written; it must be >= pad_to_size for the call to succeed.
pad_to_size specifies the exact number of bytes to write; the encoding will fail if value cannot be encoded within this exact size.
coded_size must be a non-NULL pointer; on success, *coded_size will equal pad_to_size.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates failure and coded_size/coded_value contents are not guaranteed to be meaningful.

functions.name: aom_img_alloc
functions.signature: aom_image_t *aom_img_alloc(aom_image_t *img, aom_img_fmt_t fmt, unsigned int d_w, unsigned int d_h, unsigned int align);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an aom_image_t descriptor and heap-backed image buffers for the given format and dimensions. If img is non-NULL, it initializes that storage; otherwise the descriptor itself is heap-allocated. Intended for creating an image to read/write pixel data and pass to encode/decode APIs.
requirements: img may be NULL to request heap allocation for the descriptor; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for aom_image_t.
align (buffer and row alignment, in bytes) must be <= 65536.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect allocation failure.
On success, the returned aom_image_t must be released with aom_img_free().

functions.name: aom_img_wrap
functions.signature: aom_image_t *aom_img_wrap(aom_image_t *img, aom_img_fmt_t fmt, unsigned int d_w, unsigned int d_h, unsigned int stride_align, unsigned char *img_data);
functions.description: Initializes an aom_image_t descriptor that wraps caller-managed image storage. No pixel memory is allocated by the function; it configures the descriptor to point into img_data using the specified format, dimensions, and stride alignment. Useful when the image buffer is owned externally.
requirements: img may be NULL to request heap allocation for the descriptor; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for aom_image_t.
fmt must be a supported aom_img_fmt_t value.
stride_align (row alignment, in bytes) must be <= 65536.

img_data must point to a buffer large enough for the specified fmt, d_w, d_h, and stride_align; the minimum size is described by the allocation math in the header note (see img_alloc_helper in libaom).
The storage pointed to by img_data must outlive the aom_image_t and remain valid until after aom_img_free() is called on the descriptor.

To determine x_chroma_shift, y_chroma_shift, and bps needed for sizing, you may call aom_img_wrap with a non-NULL descriptor and a sentinel non-NULL img_data (e.g., (unsigned char*)1), compute size, then call again with a valid buffer; do not use the descriptor with other APIs until after a successful call with a valid image buffer.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect allocation failure.
On success, the descriptor should later be passed to aom_img_free(); aom_img_free will not free caller-owned img_data.

functions.name: aom_img_alloc_with_border
functions.signature: aom_image_t *aom_img_alloc_with_border(aom_image_t *img, aom_img_fmt_t fmt, unsigned int d_w, unsigned int d_h, unsigned int align, unsigned int size_align, unsigned int border);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes an aom_image_t and heap-backed image buffers including a padded border on all four sides. Useful when encoders/filters require border padding for motion compensation or convolution.
requirements: img may be NULL to request heap allocation for the descriptor; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for aom_image_t.
align (buffer and row alignment, in bytes) must be <= 65536.
size_align (pixel alignment for width/height) must be <= 65536.
border (pixels padded on all sides) must be <= 65536.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect allocation failure.
On success, the returned aom_image_t must be released with aom_img_free().

functions.name: aom_img_set_rect
functions.signature: int aom_img_set_rect(aom_image_t *img, unsigned int x, unsigned int y, unsigned int w, unsigned int h, unsigned int border);
functions.description: Sets the displayed rectangle (viewport) within the image buffer by updating d_w, d_h, and plane pointers/offsets. Returns 0 if the rectangle is valid, otherwise nonzero (-1). Use to crop or select a sub-viewport of an existing image including border considerations.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized aom_image_t.
x, y, w, h must describe a rectangle that is valid within the underlying image storage; function returns -1 if invalid.
border should match the border configuration of the image (as allocated or wrapped).
Caller must check the return value and handle nonzero (-1) as an error.

functions.name: aom_img_flip
functions.description: Adjusts plane pointers and strides to vertically flip the image in-place (top becomes bottom) without moving pixels. Useful for changing image origin convention.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized aom_image_t.

functions.name: aom_img_free
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with an aom_image_t. Frees heap-allocated descriptor and/or image buffers as appropriate. Safe to call on images allocated via aom_img_alloc, aom_img_alloc_with_border, or aom_img_wrap (only descriptor/internal state is freed; caller-owned img_data is not freed).
requirements: img may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to an aom_image_t previously initialized by aom_img_alloc, aom_img_alloc_with_border, or aom_img_wrap.
After this call, the aom_image_t must not be used.

functions.name: aom_img_plane_width
functions.description: Returns the width, in pixels, of the specified plane for the image, accounting for subsampling. Useful for iterating over per-plane buffers.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized aom_image_t.
plane must refer to a valid plane index for the image format (e.g., AOM_PLANE_Y=0, AOM_PLANE_U=1, AOM_PLANE_V=2; note NV12 has no separate V plane).

functions.name: aom_img_plane_height
functions.description: Returns the height, in pixels, of the specified plane for the image, accounting for subsampling. Useful for iterating over per-plane buffers.
requirements: img must be a valid, initialized aom_image_t.
plane must refer to a valid plane index for the image format (e.g., AOM_PLANE_Y=0, AOM_PLANE_U=1, AOM_PLANE_V=2; note NV12 has no separate V plane).

functions.name: aom_img_add_metadata
functions.signature: int aom_img_add_metadata(aom_image_t *img, uint32_t type, const uint8_t *data, size_t sz, aom_metadata_insert_flags_t insert_flag);
functions.description: Appends a metadata payload to the image’s metadata array. The function allocates and stores a copy of the provided data and records the type and desired insertion behavior (insert_flag) for encoding. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: img must be a valid aom_image_t.
data must be non-NULL.
sz must be > 0.
Caller must handle return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates error (img or data NULL, sz == 0, or memory allocation failure).
insert_flag controls placement/layer-specific behavior during encode; choose from aom_metadata_insert_flags_t.

functions.name: aom_img_get_metadata
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the metadata payload at the given index in the image’s metadata array. Returns NULL if img and/or index is invalid.
requirements: img must be a valid aom_image_t with a metadata array.
index must be within the number of metadata elements; otherwise NULL is returned.
Returned pointer is const; do not modify or free it directly (use aom_img_remove_metadata or aom_img_metadata_free on individually allocated metadata when appropriate).

functions.name: aom_img_num_metadata
functions.description: Returns the number of metadata blocks stored in the image. Returns 0 if img or its metadata array is NULL.
requirements: img may be NULL; if NULL or if img->metadata is NULL, the function returns 0.
Use result to bound valid indices for aom_img_get_metadata.

functions.name: aom_img_remove_metadata
functions.description: Removes and frees all metadata associated with the image and sets the image’s metadata pointer to NULL.
requirements: img must be a valid aom_image_t.
After this call, img->metadata becomes NULL and previous metadata pointers obtained via aom_img_get_metadata are invalid.

functions.name: aom_img_metadata_alloc
functions.signature: aom_metadata_t *aom_img_metadata_alloc(uint32_t type, const uint8_t *data, size_t sz, aom_metadata_insert_flags_t insert_flag);
functions.description: Allocates a new aom_metadata_t, allocates a payload buffer of size sz, copies sz bytes from data into the payload, and sets the type and insert_flag. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: data must be non-NULL.
sz must be > 0.
Caller must check the returned pointer for NULL to detect allocation failure.
The returned aom_metadata_t must be freed with aom_img_metadata_free().

functions.name: aom_img_metadata_free
functions.description: Frees an aom_metadata_t and its associated payload buffer.
requirements: metadata may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a metadata object allocated by aom_img_metadata_alloc or owned by the image’s metadata array.
After this call, metadata must not be used.

functions.name: aom_codec_version
functions.description: Returns a packed integer encoding of the library major.minor.patch version. Intended for compile/runtime checks or logging.

functions.name: aom_codec_version_str
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string containing the full library version (may include additional qualifiers like rc tags).
requirements: > Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: aom_codec_version_extra_str
functions.description: Returns the “extra” string portion of the version (the part after the three-digit major.minor.patch).
requirements: > Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: aom_codec_build_config
functions.description: Returns a string describing the library build configuration, useful for support/diagnostics.
requirements: > Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: aom_codec_iface_name
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for the given codec interface object.
requirements: > iface must point to a valid codec interface obtained from the library (e.g., aom_codec_av1_cx()/aom_codec_av1_dx()).
> Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: aom_codec_err_to_string
functions.description: Converts an aom_codec_err_t value to a one-line human-readable string.
requirements: > The returned string contains no newline characters.
> Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not modify or free.

functions.name: aom_codec_error
functions.description: Returns a one-line human-readable description of the last error for the given codec context.
requirements: > ctx must point to a valid aom_codec_ctx_t (initialized or previously used).
> Returned string contains no newline characters.
> Returned pointer refers to static storage valid for the lifetime of the library; do not modify or free.

functions.name: aom_codec_error_detail
functions.description: Returns a detailed error string for the last error on the codec context. The string is only valid until the next aom_codec_* call on the same context.
requirements: > ctx must point to a valid aom_codec_ctx_t.
> The returned pointer may be NULL if no detailed information is available.
> The returned string is only valid until the next aom_codec_* function call (except aom_codec_error/aom_codec_error_detail); copy it if it must persist.

functions.name: aom_codec_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a codec instance and frees associated resources.
requirements: > ctx must be non-NULL; passing NULL results in AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM.
> ctx should reference an initialized codec context; destroying an uninitialized context may return AOM_CODEC_ERROR.
> Must be called once for each successfully initialized aom_codec_ctx_t to avoid leaks.

functions.name: aom_codec_get_caps
functions.description: Returns the capability bitfield for the given codec interface (AOM_CODEC_CAP_* flags).
requirements: > iface must point to a valid codec interface from the library.

functions.name: aom_codec_control
functions.description: Issues a codec-specific control command. ctrl_id selects the control (defined in aom.h/aomcx.h/aomdx.h). The variadic argument’s type and meaning depend on ctrl_id; for getters it is typically a pointer that the codec will write to, for setters it is a value or pointer as specified by the control’s documentation.
requirements: > ctx must point to an initialized codec context.
> ctrl_id must be nonzero.
> The variadic argument must match the type required by ctrl_id (see control ID documentation).
> For getter-style controls, any output pointer must be non-NULL and point to writable storage of the correct type/size.
> On error, if ctx is non-NULL, ctx->err is set to the return value.
> If using AOM_CODEC_CONTROL_TYPECHECKED, the id must be a literal in the macro and the argument type must match.

functions.name: aom_codec_set_option
functions.signature: aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_set_option(aom_codec_ctx_t *ctx, const char *name, const char *value);
functions.description: Sets a codec option using a key/value interface. Useful for configuring features by name.
requirements: > ctx must point to an initialized codec context.
> name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string naming a supported option.
> value must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing the option value.
> Returns AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM if the data is not valid; returns AOM_CODEC_ERROR if the option could not be set.

functions.name: aom_obu_type_to_string
functions.description: Converts an OBU_TYPE enum value to its string name.
requirements: > Returned pointer refers to static storage; do not modify or free.
> Passing an unknown/unsupported type may return a generic or implementation-defined string.

functions.name: aom_codec_dec_init_ver
functions.signature: aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_dec_init_ver(aom_codec_ctx_t *ctx, aom_codec_iface_t *iface, const aom_codec_dec_cfg_t *cfg, aom_codec_flags_t flags, int ver);
functions.description: Initializes a decoder context for a given codec interface. Use this to create a decoding instance, optionally providing configuration and feature flags. Normally applications should use the aom_codec_dec_init macro, which supplies the correct ABI version. Not thread-safe if the library was built without internal multithreading support; in that case, guard with a lock when used concurrently.
requirements: ctx must be a valid non-NULL pointer to an aom_codec_ctx_t to be initialized.
iface must be a valid non-NULL pointer to a decoder algorithm interface (aom_codec_iface_t).
cfg may be NULL; if non-NULL, fields should be set appropriately (e.g., threads, w, h, allow_lowbitdepth).
flags is a bitfield of AOM_CODEC_USE_* flags; pass 0 if no special features are needed.
ver must equal AOM_DECODER_ABI_VERSION.
Call this before calling any other decode operations on ctx.
If the library was built with CONFIG_MULTITHREAD=0, calls to this function are not thread-safe and must be externally synchronized.
On success returns AOM_CODEC_OK; on allocation failure may return AOM_CODEC_MEM_ERROR.

functions.name: aom_codec_peek_stream_info
functions.signature: aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_peek_stream_info(aom_codec_iface_t *iface, const uint8_t *data, size_t data_sz, aom_codec_stream_info_t *si);
functions.description: Parses a block of coded data to quickly determine if it is a supported bitstream and to extract high-level stream properties without creating a decoder instance. Updates fields in si based on the bitstream.
requirements: iface must be a valid non-NULL decoder interface pointer for the target bitstream.
data must be a valid non-NULL pointer to coded data.
data_sz must be the size in bytes of data and should be greater than 0; insufficient size may yield AOM_CODEC_UNSUP_BITSTREAM.
si must be a valid non-NULL pointer; si->is_annexb MUST be properly initialized by the caller before calling; other fields will be set by this function.
Returns AOM_CODEC_OK on success; AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM if any argument is invalid; AOM_CODEC_UNSUP_BITSTREAM if the data is unrecognized or too short.

functions.name: aom_codec_get_stream_info
functions.description: Retrieves stream information that has been parsed during decoding of data submitted to the decoder context. Populates si with properties of the current stream.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context created with aom_codec_dec_init_ver/aom_codec_dec_init.
si must be a valid non-NULL pointer to aom_codec_stream_info_t that will be updated.
Returns AOM_CODEC_OK on success; AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM for invalid inputs; AOM_CODEC_UNSUP_BITSTREAM if the submitted data could not be parsed.

functions.name: aom_codec_decode
functions.signature: aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_decode(aom_codec_ctx_t *ctx, const uint8_t *data, size_t data_sz, void *user_priv);
functions.description: Submits a buffer of coded video data to the decoder for processing. Input frames must be provided in decode-time-stamp (DTS) order. Decoded frames become available for display in presentation-time-stamp (PTS) order via aom_codec_get_frame.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
data must point to a valid buffer of coded data; the buffer must contain data_sz bytes.
data_sz must accurately reflect the number of bytes available at data.
Input coded data MUST be supplied in DTS order.
user_priv is opaque per-frame user data and may be NULL; it is associated with the frame.
On success returns AOM_CODEC_OK; otherwise returns an ::aom_codec_err_t error code indicating recoverability.

functions.name: aom_codec_get_frame
functions.description: Iterates over decoded frames ready for display after a decode call. Initialize *iter to NULL before the first call to start iteration; continue calling until NULL is returned, which indicates no more frames are available. The available frame list is valid after aom_codec_decode completes and remains valid until the next call to aom_codec_decode.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context and should have had a prior call to aom_codec_decode that produced output.
iter must be a valid pointer to iterator storage and must be initialized to NULL before the first call in an iteration sequence.
Do not modify iter except by passing it back to this function between successive calls in the same iteration.
Frames are returned in PTS order; stop when the function returns NULL.

functions.name: aom_codec_set_frame_buffer_functions
functions.signature: aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_set_frame_buffer_functions(aom_codec_ctx_t *ctx, aom_get_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t cb_get, aom_release_frame_buffer_cb_fn_t cb_release, void *cb_priv);
functions.description: Registers application-supplied callbacks for obtaining and releasing external frame buffers used by the decoder. Must be called before the first decode to switch the decoder to use external buffers instead of internally-allocated ones. Only valid for decoders that advertise AOM_CODEC_CAP_EXTERNAL_FRAME_BUFFER. For AV1 decoding, applications may need to provide at least AOM_MAXIMUM_WORK_BUFFERS buffers.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized decoder context.
cb_get must be a valid non-NULL callback that provides a frame buffer on demand.
cb_release must be a valid non-NULL callback that releases a frame buffer when no longer referenced internally.
cb_priv is an opaque pointer passed to the callbacks and may be NULL.
This function MUST be called before the first call to aom_codec_decode if external frame buffers are to be used.
Only call this when the decoder interface advertises AOM_CODEC_CAP_EXTERNAL_FRAME_BUFFER; otherwise the call will fail with AOM_CODEC_INCAPABLE.

Returns AOM_CODEC_OK on success; AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM if any required callback is NULL; AOM_CODEC_ERROR if the decoder context is not initialized; AOM_CODEC_INCAPABLE if the algorithm does not support external frame buffers.

functions.name: aom_codec_dec_init
functions.signature: aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_dec_init(aom_codec_ctx_t *ctx, aom_codec_iface_t *iface, const aom_codec_dec_cfg_t *cfg, aom_codec_flags_t flags)
functions.description: Convenience initializer for a decoder context. This is a macro that calls aom_codec_dec_init_ver(...) with ver set to AOM_DECODER_ABI_VERSION. Use it to initialize an aom_codec_ctx_t with a specific decoder interface (aom_codec_iface_t), optional decoder configuration, and AOM_CODEC_USE_* flags. Returns AOM_CODEC_OK on success or an error code on failure. Typical usage: allocate an aom_codec_ctx_t, then call aom_codec_dec_init(&ctx, iface, cfg, flags) before submitting bitstream data to aom_codec_decode.
requirements: ctx must be a valid pointer to a decoder context object to be initialized.
iface must be a valid pointer to a decoder algorithm interface (aom_codec_iface_t).
cfg may be NULL; when non-NULL it supplies initialization parameters (threads, width/height, allow_lowbitdepth).
flags is a bitfield of AOM_CODEC_USE_* flags.
When the library is built with CONFIG_MULTITHREAD=0, this call is not thread-safe and must be guarded by a lock in multithreaded contexts.
Must be called before any decoding operations (e.g., before aom_codec_decode).
On success, the context is initialized; callers should check the return value for AOM_CODEC_OK and handle other aom_codec_err_t codes (e.g., AOM_CODEC_MEM_ERROR) appropriately.

functions.name: aom_codec_av1_dx
functions.description: Returns the interface descriptor for the AV1 decoder. Typically used by passing the returned aom_codec_iface_t* to aom_codec_dec_init() (or aom_codec_init()) to initialize a decoder context for AV1 bitstreams. The returned interface is a static, library-owned object and is not to be modified or freed by the caller.
requirements: Must be used with the AOM codec initialization APIs (e.g., aom_codec_dec_init) that expect an aom_codec_iface_t*.
Caller must not free or modify the returned interface pointer (library-owned, static lifetime).
Library must be built/linked with AV1 decoder support; otherwise initialization with this interface may fail.

functions.name: aom_inspect_cb
functions.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked to inspect decoder frame data. Implementations of this callback can be registered via the AV1_SET_INSPECTION_CALLBACK control (when supported) to receive per-frame decode inspection notifications. Note: This is a callback type definition, not an exported function symbol. Parameter semantics beyond their types are not documented here; decoder is an opaque decoder pointer and ctx is the user-provided context.
requirements: The function must match the exact signature: void (*)(void *decoder, void *ctx).
The decoder argument will be provided by the library; treat it as opaque unless using documented inspection APIs. Specific structure and lifetime are unknown.
The ctx argument is the user-supplied context passed during registration (via AV1_SET_INSPECTION_CALLBACK).
When the library is built without inspection support (CONFIG_INSPECTION=0), attempts to register this callback via AV1_SET_INSPECTION_CALLBACK return AOM_CODEC_INCAPABLE (callback will not be used).
The callback implementation must be reentrant/thread-safe if the decoder invokes it from multithreaded decode paths (threading behavior is not specified here).

functions.name: aom_codec_enc_init_ver
functions.description: Initialize an encoder context with the given codec interface, optional configuration, and feature flags. Typical usage is via the aom_codec_enc_init macro which supplies the correct ABI version. If initialization fails, you do not need to call aom_codec_destroy() on ctx. Note: If the library was built with CONFIG_MULTITHREAD=0, this call is not thread-safe and must be externally synchronized in multithreaded scenarios.
requirements: ctx must point to an encoder context structure to be initialized (non-NULL).
iface must reference a valid encoder algorithm interface (non-NULL).
cfg may be NULL (configuration to use, if known).
flags is a bitfield of AOM_CODEC_USE_* flags.
ver must equal AOM_ENCODER_ABI_VERSION.
If the library was configured with CONFIG_MULTITHREAD=0, callers must guard this call with a lock when used from multiple threads.
On failure, callers are not required to call aom_codec_destroy() on ctx.

functions.name: aom_codec_enc_config_default
functions.description: Populate an encoder configuration with codec-specific default values for the requested usage profile. This should be called before customizing cfg for encoding.
requirements: iface must reference an encoder interface; otherwise returns AOM_CODEC_INCAPABLE.
cfg must be non-NULL; otherwise returns AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM.
usage must be recognized by the codec. For AV1, usage must be AOM_USAGE_GOOD_QUALITY (0), AOM_USAGE_REALTIME (1), or AOM_USAGE_ALL_INTRA (2); otherwise returns AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM.

functions.name: aom_codec_enc_config_set
functions.description: Reconfigure an initialized encoder instance using the supplied configuration structure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context (non-NULL).
cfg must be non-NULL; otherwise returns AOM_CODEC_INVALID_PARAM.
iface backing ctx must be an encoder interface; otherwise returns AOM_CODEC_INCAPABLE.

functions.name: aom_codec_get_global_headers
functions.description: Retrieve a global stream header packet, if supported by the codec. For AV1, returns a Low Overhead Bitstream Format OBU with obu_has_size_field set. Call this only after all configuration is finalized.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context (non-NULL).
Calls to this function should be deferred until all configuration has been passed to the encoder; otherwise the returned header may be invalidated by later changes.
On success, the caller owns and must free both the returned aom_fixed_buf_t pointer and its buf member using free().
May return NULL if unsupported or on error; callers must handle NULL.

functions.name: aom_codec_encode
functions.description: Encode a frame at the given presentation timestamp (PTS). Pass img as NULL repeatedly to flush delayed frames at end-of-stream; encoding is complete when subsequent aom_codec_get_cx_data() calls return no data. The function may modify img->planes when denoising is enabled, despite img being const.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context (non-NULL).
PTS values must be strictly increasing across successive non-NULL frames.
If img is not NULL: duration must be nonzero and must be <= UINT32_MAX.
If img is NULL: pts and duration are ignored (use to flush).
Pixel sample values in img must be within [0 .. (1 << img->bit_depth) - 1]; encoding values outside this range is undefined behavior.
If AV1E_SET_DENOISE_NOISE_LEVEL is set to a nonzero value, the encoder may modify img->planes; callers must not rely on img data remaining unchanged in this case.
flags is a bitfield of per-frame flags (e.g., AOM_EFLAG_*).

functions.name: aom_codec_set_cx_data_buf
functions.signature:
aom_codec_err_t aom_codec_set_cx_data_buf(aom_codec_ctx_t *ctx,
                                          const aom_fixed_buf_t *buf,
                                          unsigned int pad_before,
                                          unsigned int pad_after);
functions.description: Provide an application-owned buffer for the next compressed frame packet and subsequent appends. The encoder writes compressed data into the buffer after pad_before bytes and appends pad_after bytes of preserved padding. If output will not fit, the encoder may return a packet that points to an internal buffer (no padding); the application must handle copying in that case. Call with buf=NULL to restore default internal-buffer behavior.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context (non-NULL).
buf may be NULL to restore default behavior; otherwise must point to a valid fixed-size buffer whose lifetime spans encoding until the application resets it.
Applications must not call this function while iterating aom_codec_get_cx_data().
pad_before and pad_after specify byte counts that the application must provision in the supplied buffer.
Because output may exceed the provided buffer, callers must be prepared for returned packets to reference internal buffers without padding and handle copying as needed.
Applications should periodically reset this buffer after consuming/flushing accumulated output to realign the write pointer.

functions.name: aom_codec_get_cx_data
functions.description: Iterate over encoder output packets (compressed frames, two-pass stats, PSNR, etc.). Initialize *iter to NULL before the first call, then pass it back unchanged to get subsequent packets until NULL is returned.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context (non-NULL).
iter must be provided by the caller and initialized to NULL before the first call for a given drain/encode interval.
The returned packet pointer remains valid only until the next call to any aom_codec_* function; callers must copy data if it must persist longer.
Callers must silently ignore packet kinds they do not recognize.
Do not call aom_codec_set_cx_data_buf() during iteration.

functions.name: aom_codec_get_preview_frame
functions.description: Return a preview image as it would appear at the decoder, if available. The returned image buffer is owned by the encoder and must not be modified by the application.
requirements: ctx must be a valid encoder context (non-NULL).
The returned pointer may be NULL if no preview image is available; callers must handle NULL.
Callers must not write into the returned image buffer.

functions.name: aom_codec_av1_cx
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the AV1 encoder interface (aom_codec_iface_t) for use with the AOM/AV1 encoder API. Typical usage is to pass the returned interface to aom_codec_enc_init_ver (or aom_codec_enc_init) to initialize an encoder context. The interface object is owned by the library and provides encoder capabilities and controls.
requirements: Caller must pass the returned interface pointer to aom_codec_enc_init(_ver) to create an encoder context.
Do not free or modify the returned aom_codec_iface_t; its lifetime is managed by the library.
Link against libaom with encoder support enabled to obtain a valid interface.

functions.name: aom_rc_create_model_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Creates an external rate control model instance. The encoder calls this callback to let the external module allocate/initialize its model based on the provided encoding configuration and return an opaque handle via rate_ctrl_model_ptr.
requirements: priv may be used by the implementation; no specific format required (opaque).
ratectrl_config must be a valid, initialized pointer to aom_rc_config_t; fields such as frame dimensions, frame rate, bitrate, and rc_mode are set by the encoder.
rate_ctrl_model_ptr must be a valid, non-NULL pointer where the implementation writes an aom_rc_model_t handle (opaque, typically allocated by the implementation).
On success, return AOM_RC_OK; otherwise return AOM_RC_ERROR.
Caller must check the return value and only use the model handle if AOM_RC_OK is returned.
The created model must later be released via aom_rc_delete_model_cb_fn_t.

functions.name: aom_rc_send_firstpass_stats_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Provides first-pass statistics to the external rate control model. Called by the encoder to supply the per-frame stats array and count so the model can analyze content before encoding decisions.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid handle previously returned by a successful create_model callback.
first_pass_stats must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
first_pass_stats->frame_stats must point to an array of aom_rc_frame_stats_t with length equal to first_pass_stats->num_frames.
first_pass_stats->num_frames must be non-negative; for typical runs it equals the number of show frames in the video.
The implementation must not write to the stats (const).
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_send_tpl_gop_stats_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Sends TPL (temporal dependency) statistics for the current GOP to the external rate control model. Used by the encoder to inform the model about inter-frame dependency and complexity information.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid handle created by create_model.
extrc_tpl_gop_stats must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a structure defined in aom_tpl.h (contents and invariants are defined there; unknown here).
The implementation must not modify the provided stats (const).
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_get_encodeframe_decision_cb_fn_t
functions.signature: aom_rc_status_t aom_rc_get_encodeframe_decision_cb_fn_t(aom_rc_model_t rate_ctrl_model, const int frame_gop_index, aom_rc_encodeframe_decision_t *frame_decision);
functions.description: Requests the per-frame encoding decision (e.g., Q index, rdmult, optional SB-level parameters) for the current frame within the GOP from the external rate control model. The encoder supplies the frame’s index within the GOP; the model fills frame_decision.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle.
frame_gop_index is the index of the frame within the current GOP and should be >= 0.
frame_decision must be a valid, non-NULL pointer that the implementation fills.
frame_decision->q_index is required; typical range is [0..255]. The special value AOM_DEFAULT_Q (-1) may be returned to defer to the encoder’s default.
frame_decision->rdmult is required; positive integer is expected. The special value AOM_DEFAULT_RDMULT (-1) may be returned to defer to the encoder’s default.

If frame_decision->sb_params_list is provided, it should point to an array of aom_sb_params entries appropriate for the frame’s dimensions; when used, q_index values must be in [0..255] and rdmult non-negative per SB. It is optional, zero-initialized by default, and typically set for key and ARF frames, not leaf frames.
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_update_encodeframe_result_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Notifies the external rate control model of the actual encoding outcome for a frame (bit count and actual qindex used). Enables the model to update its internal state/feedback loop.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle.
encode_frame_result must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
encode_frame_result->bit_count should be >= 0 (number of bits used).
encode_frame_result->actual_encoding_qindex should be within [0..255].
The implementation must not modify the provided result (const).
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_get_key_frame_decision_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Obtains the key-frame placement decision from the external rate control model. The model specifies the next key frame’s show index and the size of its key-frame group.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle.
key_frame_decision must be a valid, non-NULL pointer that the implementation fills.
key_frame_decision->key_frame_show_index should be >= 0 (index in the video).
key_frame_decision->key_frame_group_size should be > 0 (number of show frames in the key-frame group).
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_get_gop_decision_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Retrieves the GOP structure decision(s) from the external rate control model. The model fills out the GOP’s show frame count, order offsets, base Q ratio, and a list of frames with their types, indices, references, and refresh behavior.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle.
gop_decision must be a valid, non-NULL pointer that the implementation fills.
gop_decision->show_frame_count should be >= 0; represents visible frames in the GOP.
gop_decision->gop_frame_list must point to an array of aom_rc_gop_frame_t of length gop_decision->gop_frame_count when returned.

Within each aom_rc_gop_frame_t: order_idx and coding_idx start at 0 within the GOP; display_idx is the number of displayed frames preceding this frame in the GOP; is_key_frame is boolean; update_type must be one of aom_rc_frame_update_type values; colocated_ref_idx is -1 unless overlay/show_existing; update_ref_idx is -1 if not updating a ref slot; extra_refresh_frame_flags is -1 if not set; layer_depth is an integer layer depth (expected within [0..AOM_RC_MAX_ARF_LAYERS], exact limit not enforced here); primary_ref_frame is a single reference descriptor; ref_frame_list contains up to AOM_RC_MAX_REF_FRAMES entries with indices and names.
If fields specify -1 as sentinel values (per comments), use -1 to indicate not applicable; otherwise provide valid indices/names.
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_get_frame_rdmult_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Asks the external rate control model for the frame-level rate–distortion multiplier (rdmult) given the encoder-provided frame information. The model writes the chosen rdmult to the output pointer.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid model handle.
frame_info must be a valid, non-NULL pointer populated by the encoder (frame type, indices, GOP info, reference validity, GOP size, use_alt_ref).
rdmult must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to int which the implementation sets. It may be set to AOM_DEFAULT_RDMULT (-1) to defer to the encoder default; otherwise should be a non-negative integer.
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_rc_delete_model_cb_fn_t
functions.description: Destroys/releases the external rate control model created earlier. The encoder calls this to allow the external module to free any resources associated with the model handle.
requirements: rate_ctrl_model must be a valid handle previously returned by a successful create_model.
Should be called once per model instance when the model is no longer needed; after return, the handle must not be used again.
Return AOM_RC_OK on success; otherwise AOM_RC_ERROR. Caller must check return value.

functions.name: aom_ext_part_create_model_fn_t
functions.description: Callback used by the encoder to create an external partition model instance. The implementation should allocate/initialize any model state and return an opaque handle via ext_part_model. Typical usage: the application registers a function of this signature; the encoder calls it once (per encoder instance or sequence as needed) before sending features/requests.
requirements: priv is a caller-provided opaque pointer; implementation must treat it as read-only context.
part_config must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; part_config->superblock_size is either 64 or 128 (representing 64x64 or 128x128).
ext_part_model must be a valid, non-NULL output pointer; on success, *ext_part_model is set to an initialized, opaque model handle usable by other callbacks.
Return AOM_EXT_PART_OK on success; return AOM_EXT_PART_ERROR (or other non-OK) on failure; callers are expected to check the return value.
Must be called before any send_features, get_partition_decision, send_partition_stats, or delete_model that use the created handle.

functions.name: aom_ext_part_send_features_fn_t
functions.description: Callback used by the encoder to provide per-block or per-superblock features to the external model so it can make partition decisions. The features structure includes multiple feature sets and context fields; the active stage is indicated by the id field.
requirements: ext_part_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by a successful aom_ext_part_create_model_fn_t call.
part_features must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; fields and arrays must conform to the sizes defined in this header (e.g., AOM_EXT_PART_SIZE_*).
The id field in part_features indicates which sub-feature group(s) are relevant at this call; implementation should read only documented fields or check id accordingly.
This function should not modify the data pointed to by part_features (parameter is const).
Return AOM_EXT_PART_OK on success; callers are expected to check the return value before calling get_partition_decision.

functions.name: aom_ext_part_get_decision_fn_t
functions.description: Callback used by the encoder to retrieve partition decisions from the external model after features have been sent. Depending on the chosen decision_mode, this may return a whole-tree decision or a per-block decision/pruning directives.
requirements: ext_part_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by a successful aom_ext_part_create_model_fn_t call.
ext_part_decision must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable storage; implementation writes the decision fields (e.g., current_decision, pruning flags, or whole-tree data).
The returned decisions must respect the semantics described by aom_partition_decision_t (e.g., use valid ranges/flags, num_nodes within array bounds).
Return AOM_EXT_PART_OK on success; callers must check the return value before using ext_part_decision contents.

functions.name: aom_ext_part_send_partition_stats_fn_t
functions.description: Callback used by the encoder to send encoding statistics (rate, distortion, rd-cost) corresponding to chosen partition(s) to the external model for training, feedback, or adaptive inference.
requirements: ext_part_model must be a valid model handle previously returned by a successful aom_ext_part_create_model_fn_t call.
ext_part_stats must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; fields (rate, dist, rdcost) must be initialized by the caller.
This function must not modify the data pointed to by ext_part_stats (parameter is const).
Return AOM_EXT_PART_OK on success; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: aom_ext_part_delete_model_fn_t
functions.description: Callback used by the encoder to destroy and release resources associated with a previously created external partition model handle.
requirements: ext_part_model must be a valid handle previously obtained from aom_ext_part_create_model_fn_t.
Implementation must free/release all resources associated with ext_part_model and invalidate the handle for further use.
Return AOM_EXT_PART_OK on successful teardown; callers should check the return value and must not use the handle after a successful delete.

unharnessable_functions.name: aom_codec_dec_init_ver
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid aom_codec_iface_t from libaom (e.g., aom_codec_av1_dx()) and ABI version constant, neither of which can be safely constructed or obtained in this harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: aom_codec_peek_stream_info

import random
from typing import List

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _uleb128_encode(value: int) -> bytes:
    # Standard unsigned LEB128 encoding for 64-bit values
    if value < 0:
        value = 0
    value &= (1 << 64) - 1
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        byte = value & 0x7F
        value >>= 7
        if value:
            out.append(byte | 0x80)
        else:
            out.append(byte)
            break
    return bytes(out)

def _interesting_uleb_values() -> List[int]:
    # Values that exercise 1..10-byte encodings and boundary cases
    vals = [
        0,
        1,
        0x7F,                 # max 1-byte
        0x80,                 # requires 2 bytes
        (1 << 14) - 1,        # max 2-byte
        1 << 14,              # 3-byte
        (1 << 21) - 1,        # max 3-byte
        1 << 21,              # 4-byte
        (1 << 28) - 1,        # max 4-byte
        1 << 28,              # 5-byte
        (1 << 35) - 1,        # max 5-byte
        1 << 35,              # 6-byte
        (1 << 42) - 1,        # max 6-byte
        1 << 42,              # 7-byte
        (1 << 49) - 1,        # max 7-byte
        1 << 49,              # 8-byte
        (1 << 56) - 1,        # max 8-byte
        1 << 56,              # 9-byte
        (1 << 63) - 1,        # large positive within 64-bit
        (1 << 64) - 1,        # max uint64 -> will use 10 bytes
    ]
    return vals

def _make_valid_leb_stream(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose a stream of several valid ULEB128 integers concatenated.
    # This is ideal for aom_uleb_decode with varying available windows.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Choose 1..6 values to keep buffer moderate
    count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    interesting = _interesting_uleb_values()
    for _ in range(count):
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            v = rng.choice(interesting)
        else:
            # random 64-bit value
            v = rng.getrandbits(64)
        enc = _uleb128_encode(v)
        parts.append(enc)
        # Occasionally insert a small random non-LEB padding region that still decodes as a value
        # by appending a single-byte ULEB (0..127), which remains valid.
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            parts.append(bytes([rng.randrange(0, 128)]))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > max_len:
        data = data[:max_len]
    return data

def _make_metadata_payload(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a payload that looks like plausible metadata content: mixture of ASCII header and random bytes
    # Ensure non-zero length as required by API users.
    # Structure: [tag][len-uleb][body], but overall just bytes; fuzzer stub treats as opaque.
    tag_choices = [b"ITUT-T35", b"HDR-CLL", b"HDR-MDCV", b"TIMECODE", b"SCALABILITY", b"USER-DATA"]
    tag = rng.choice(tag_choices)
    # Random body length up to target_len - minimal overhead
    min_overhead = len(tag) + 2  # include a small separator and at least one LEB byte
    body_len = max(0, target_len - min_overhead)
    # Vary actual body length a bit
    body_len = rng.randint(max(0, body_len // 2), body_len) if body_len > 0 else 0
    body = _rand_bytes(rng, body_len)
    leb = _uleb128_encode(len(body))
    buf = tag + b"\x00" + leb + body
    # If still shorter than target, append some deterministic pattern bytes
    if len(buf) < target_len:
        pad = target_len - len(buf)
        pattern = bytes((i % 256 for i in range(pad)))
        buf += pattern
    return buf

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide which target we prioritize for this buffer:
    # 0 -> ULEB stream (good for aom_uleb_decode FUZZ_PARAM_STR)
    # 1 -> metadata payload (good for aom_img_add_metadata / aom_img_metadata_alloc FUZZ_PARAM_STR)
    mode = rng.randrange(0, 2)

    # Limit overall size to <= 4096 bytes
    max_size = 4096

    if mode == 0:
        # Build a buffer with concatenated valid ULEB128 numbers and ensure multiple boundaries
        buf = _make_valid_leb_stream(rng, max_size)
        # Ensure non-empty
        if not buf:
            buf = bytes([0])
        return buf
    else:
        # Construct a rich metadata payload of moderate size to avoid excessive allocations.
        # Choose a target size in [32, 1024]
        target_len = rng.randint(32, 1024)
        buf = _make_metadata_payload(rng, target_len)
        # Ensure non-empty
        if not buf:
            buf = b"\x01"
        # Cap length defensively
        if len(buf) > max_size:
            buf = buf[:max_size]
        return buf

# This generator focuses on producing interesting key/value strings for aom_codec_set_option.
# The fuzzer stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() twice to obtain name and value. We therefore
# concatenate two NUL-terminated strings: name\0value\0. The harness should split them.
# We provide a diverse set of plausible option names and values used by libaom AV1 encoder/decoder
# option interface (string-based). All outputs are valid C strings and <= 4096 bytes.

    "is-annexb", "invert-tile-decode-order", "skip-loop-filter",

# Enumerated value pools for specific options; we also include numeric strings and booleans
ENUM_VALUES = {
    "usage": ["good", "rt", "allintra", "0", "1", "2"],
    "end-usage": ["vbr", "cbr", "cq", "q", "0", "1", "2", "3"],
    "bit-depth": ["8", "10", "12"],
    "tune": ["psnr", "ssim", "vmaf_with_preprocessing", "vmaf_without_preprocessing"],

    "color-range": ["studio", "full", "0", "1"],
    "color-primaries": ["bt709", "bt601", "bt2020", "unspecified", "1", "6", "9", "2"],
    "transfer-characteristics": ["bt709", "srgb", "pq", "hlg", "1", "13", "16", "18"],
    "matrix-coefficients": ["identity", "bt709", "bt601", "bt2020_ncl", "0", "1", "6", "9"],

}

BOOL_VALUES = ["0", "1", "true", "false", "on", "off", "yes", "no"]

# Numeric ranges of interest for integer-like options
INT_RANGES = {
    "cpu-used": (-8, 9),
    "threads": (1, 64),
    "tile-columns": (0, 6),
    "tile-rows": (0, 6),
    "row-mt": (0, 1),
    "deltaq-mode": (0, 3),
    "lag-in-frames": (0, 35),
    "target-bitrate": (1, 50000),
    "undershoot-pct": (0, 100),
    "overshoot-pct": (0, 100),
    "min-q": (0, 63),
    "max-q": (0, 63),
    "superres-denom": (8, 16),
    "superres-kf-denom": (8, 16),
    "kf-max-dist": (0, 9999),
    "kf-min-dist": (0, 9999),
    "row-mt-unit-test": (0, 1),
}

# Some composite/compound values like WxH or timebase num/den
COMPOSITE_GENERATORS: List[Tuple[str, callable]] = [
    ("render-size", lambda rng: f"{rng.randint(16,3840)}x{rng.randint(16,2160)}"),
]

# Fallback random token generator
ALPHA = string.ascii_letters
ALPHANUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_/.:+"


def pick_value_for(name: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lname = name.lower()
    # Enumerated textual values
    if lname in ENUM_VALUES:
        return rng.choice(ENUM_VALUES[lname])
    # Boolean-like toggles
    if any(tok in lname for tok in ["enable", "allow", "skip", "invert", "annexb", "lossless", "denoise", "row-mt"]):
        return rng.choice(BOOL_VALUES)
    # Integer-like ranges
    if lname in INT_RANGES:
        lo, hi = INT_RANGES[lname]
        val = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        return str(val)
    # Composite patterns
    for key, gen in COMPOSITE_GENERATORS:
        if key in lname:
            return gen(rng)
    # Generic numeric or token
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 10000))
    elif choice == 1:
        return f"{rng.randint(0,255)},{rng.randint(0,255)},{rng.randint(0,255)}"
    elif choice == 2:
        return rng.choice(BOOL_VALUES)
    else:
        # short token
        ln = rng.randint(2, 12)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(ALPHANUM) for _ in range(ln))


def pick_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Bias toward known names, but also generate unknowns to explore option parser
    if rng.random() < 0.85:
        return rng.choice(OPTION_NAMES)
    # Unknown but plausible name: lowercase with dashes
    parts = rng.randint(1, 3)
    segs = []
    for _ in range(parts):
        ln = rng.randint(3, 10)
        segs.append(''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(ln)))
    return '-'.join(segs)


def encode_c_strings(pairs: Tuple[str, str]) -> bytes:
    # name\0value\0
    name, value = pairs
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; sanitize by replacing if any
    name = name.replace('\x00', '')
    value = value.replace('\x00', '')
    return name.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00" + value.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Sometimes generate multiple concatenated pairs to seed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses across runs
    pairs_count = 1
    # Keep within size limit; occasionally provide a few extra pairs for corpus richness
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        pairs_count = rng.randint(2, 4)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(pairs_count):
        name = pick_name(rng)
        value = pick_value_for(name, rng)

        # Occasionally craft interdependent values (e.g., min-q <= max-q)
        if name == "min-q":
            minq = int(value)
            maxq = rng.randint(minq, max(minq, INT_RANGES.get("max-q", (0, 63))[1]))
            chunks.append(encode_c_strings(("min-q", str(minq))))
            chunks.append(encode_c_strings(("max-q", str(maxq))))
            continue
        if name == "max-q":
            maxq = int(value)
            minq = rng.randint(INT_RANGES.get("min-q", (0, 63))[0], maxq)
            chunks.append(encode_c_strings(("min-q", str(minq))))
            chunks.append(encode_c_strings(("max-q", str(maxq))))
            continue
        if name in ("superres-mode",):
            # If fixed, also provide denom
            if value in ("fixed", "1") and rng.random() < 0.8:
                denom = rng.randint(*INT_RANGES["superres-denom"]) if "superres-denom" in INT_RANGES else rng.randint(8,16)
                chunks.append(encode_c_strings((name, value)))
                chunks.append(encode_c_strings(("superres-denom", str(denom))))
                continue

        chunks.append(encode_c_strings((name, value)))

    data = b"".join(chunks)
    # Enforce size limit
    return data[:4096]
